name: Link Preview
title: Link Preview: See Your URL on 6 Platforms at Once
description: Free link preview tool: see how a URL looks on Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Slack, Discord and iMessage — from the tags each platform actually reads.
answer: A link preview is the card — title, description, image — that appears when you share a URL. Enter any URL to see approximately how it will look on Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Slack, Discord and iMessage at once, and which tags each preview was built from.
trust: We fetch the page once, read its Open Graph, X card and fallback tags, and render each platform's layout from the same data. Platforms change their designs, so treat the cards as close approximations.
body:
## OG Preview: How Open Graph Tags Become a Card

Every platform starts from the same tags. The [Open Graph](https://ogp.me/) title, description and image fill the card; if they're missing, platforms fall back to the page title, the meta description and whatever image they can find.

## Open Graph Preview for Facebook, LinkedIn, X and Slack

The data is shared, the layouts aren't:

| Platform | Image shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Facebook | Wide, about 1.91:1 | Small thumbnail below about 600×315 |
| LinkedIn | Wide, 1.91:1 | Minimum 1200×627 for the large layout |
| X | Wide with summary_large_image | Needs the twitter:card tag |
| Slack | Small image beside the text | Shows the site name above the title |
| Discord | Embed card | Image below the text |
| iMessage | Large image card | Title and domain under the image |

## LinkedIn Preview: Why LinkedIn Shows a Different Image

LinkedIn uses og:image only when it meets its rules — [at least 1200×627 at 1.91:1, under 5 MB](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a521928). Smaller images get a small thumbnail or are skipped. LinkedIn also caches previews: run the URL through [Post Inspector](https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/) to refresh it.

## URL Preview Before You Share It

Check before you post, because changing tags afterwards doesn't always update posts already shared. Look at three things: the title isn't a menu label, the image isn't a logo on a white square, and the description isn't a cookie notice.

## Social Share Preview: The 60-Second Checklist

Five tags fix nearly every preview:

1. og:title — written for the share, not stuffed with keywords.
2. og:description — one clear sentence.
3. og:image — 1200×630, PNG or JPEG, absolute URL.
4. og:url — the canonical URL.
5. twitter:card — summary_large_image.

Most big sites have them: in our October 2026 analysis of 315 big-brand homepages ([dataset](/resources/technical-seo-baseline-2026-10.json)), 86.7% set og:image and 74.3% chose the large X card. Create a card image with the [OG image generator](/tools/og-image-generator), and dig into individual tags with the [Open Graph checker](/tools/open-graph-checker).

faqs.q: How do I preview how a link will look when shared?
faqs.a: Enter the URL above. We read the page's Open Graph and X card tags and render approximate previews for Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Slack, Discord and iMessage side by side.

faqs.q: Why does my link show no image?
faqs.a: The og:image tag is missing, points to a file that fails to load, is too small for the platform's large layout, or uses SVG. Each platform also caches old previews.

faqs.q: How do I change the preview of a link I already shared?
faqs.a: Update the tags, then refresh the platform's cache with Meta's Sharing Debugger or LinkedIn's Post Inspector. On X, posting the link with a query string forces a new fetch.
